class.name: Champion (LotR)
class.proficiency: Strength, Constitution, Acrobatics, Animal Handling, Athletics, Intimidation, Perception, Survival
class.armor: Light Armor, Medium Armor, Heavy Armor, Shields

trait.name: Champion
trait.text:
"War must be, while we defend our lives against a destroyer who would devour all.."
You deem that there is but one way to oppose the return of the Shadow, and that it is to conquer it by strength of arms. You are recognized as a warrior among your folk, a valiant fighter, onward into battle. For you, the road to adventure leads straight to wherever your foes prowl or hide.
Source: The Lord of the Rings p. 48

feature.name: Starting Champion
feature.text:
As a 1st-level Champion, you begin play with 10 + your Constitution modifier hit points.
You are proficient with the following items, in addition to any proficiencies provided by your race or background.
• Armor: light armor, medium armor, heavy armor, shields • Weapons: simple weapons, martial weapons • Tools: none • Skills: Choose 2 from Acrobatics, Animal Handling, Athletics, Intimidation, Perception, and Hunting
You begin play with the following equipment, in addition to any equipment provided by your background.
• (a) ring-mail or (b) hide armor or (c) leather shirt, great bow, and a quiver of 20 arrows • (a) a martial weapon and a shield or (b) a martial melee weapon and a simple melee weapon • (a) a bow and a quiver of 20 arrows or (b) two simple melee weapons
If you forgo this starting equipment, as well as the items offered by your background, you start with 5d4 × 10 gp to buy your equipment.
Source: Lord of the Rings p. 48

feature.name: Multiclass Champion
feature.text:
If your group uses the optional rule on multiclassing in the Player's Handbook, here's what you need to know if you choose champion as one of your classes.
Ability Score Minimum: As a multiclass character, you must have at least 1 of the following ability score(s) to take a level in this class, or to take a level in another class if you are already a champion.
• Strength 13, or • Dexterity 13
Proficiencies Gained: When you gain your first level in a class other than your initial class, you gain only some of your new class's starting proficiencies, here are the proficiencies you gain when you take your first level as a champion.
• Armor: light armor, medium armor, heavy armor, shields • Weapons: simple weapons, martial weapons • Tools: none
Source: Lord of the Rings p. 67

feature.name: Shadow Path
feature.text:
Curse of Vengeance: Individuals who live by the sword are ever tempted to draw it, either literally or figuratively, when their will is thwarted or when they deem their honor to have been impugned by an insult. As corruption spreads in their spirit, their behavior worsens, leading to more extreme violent reactions.
Source: Lord of the Rings p. 49

feature.name: Fighting Style
feature.text:
You adopt a particular style of fighting as your speciality. Choose one of the following options. You cannot take a Fighting Style option more than once, even if you later get to choose again.
Source: Lord of the Rings p. 49

feature.name: Fighting Style: Archery
feature.text:
You gain a +2 bonus to attack rolls you make with ranged weapons.
Source: Lord of the Rings p. 49

feature.name: Fighting Style: Defense
feature.text:
While you are wearing armor, you gain a +1 bonus to AC.
Source: Lord of the Rings p. 49

feature.name: Fighting Style: Dueling
feature.text:
When you are wielding a melee weapon in one hand and no other weapons, you gain a +2 bonus to damage rolls with that weapon.
Source: Lord of the Rings p. 49

feature.name: Fighting Style: Great Weapon Fighting
feature.text:
When you roll damage for an attack you make with a melee weapon that you are wielding with two hands, you can treat any roll of 4 or less on a damage die as a 5. The weapon must have the two-handed or versatile property for you to gain this benefit.
Source: Lord of the Rings p. 49

feature.name: Fighting Style: Protection
feature.text:
When a creature you can see hits you or a target other than you that is within 5 feet of you with a melee attack, you can use your reaction to add your proficiency bonus to the target's AC for that attack, potentially causing the attack to miss. You must be wielding a shield or a finesse weapon.
Source: Lord of the Rings p. 49

feature.name: Fighting Style: Two-Weapon Fighting
feature.text:
When you engage in two-weapon fighting, you can add your ability modifier to the damage of the second attack.
Source: Lord of the Rings p. 49

feature.name: Surge of Vigour
feature.text:
You have a limited well of stamina that you can draw on to protect yourself from harm, or to push yourself beyond your normal limits for a moment. You can use a bonus action to either take the Attack, Dash, Disengage, or Dodge action, or to regain hit points equal to 1d8 + your Champion level + your Constitution modifier. Once you use this feature, you must finish a short or long rest before you can use it again.
Source: Lord of the Rings p. 49

feature.name: Virtue
feature.text:
At 2nd level, and again at 4th, 6th, and 8th level, you can take a common or cultural virtue of your choice. You can take each virtue only once. As normal, you cannot increase an ability score above 20 using this feature. At 2nd and 6th level, instead of taking a virtue you can gain a craft slot and a craft of your choice from the Scholar's Crafts list (see page 64).
Source: Lord of the Rings p. 49

feature.name: Champion Way
feature.text:
There are different ways for a Champion to follow, but all lead to confronting the enemy with fighting prowess.
At 3rd level, you choose a way that you strive to follow in your combat styles and techniques. Choose Sharp-shooter or Slayer, both detailed at the end of the calling description. The way you choose grants you features at 3rd level and again at 7th level.
Source: Lord of the Rings p. 49

feature.name: Virtue Improvement
feature.text:
At 4th level, you can take a common or cultural virtue of your choice. You can take each virtue only once. As normal, you cannot increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.
Source: Lord of the Rings p. 49

feature.name: Extra Attack
feature.text:
Beginning at 5th level, you can attack twice, instead of once, whenever you take the Attack action on your turn. The number of attacks increases to three when you reach 10th level in this calling.
Source: Lord of the Rings p. 49

feature.name: Virtue Improvement
feature.text:
At 6th level, you can take a common or cultural virtue of your choice. You can take each virtue only once. As normal, you cannot increase an ability score above 20 using this feature. At 6th level, instead of taking a virtue you can gain a craft slot and a craft of your choice from the Scholar's Crafts list (see page 64).
Source: Lord of the Rings p. 49

feature.name: Virtue Improvement
feature.text:
At 8th, you can take a common or cultural virtue of your choice. You can take each virtue only once. As normal, you cannot increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.
Source: Lord of the Rings p. 49

feature.name: Indomitable
feature.text:
At 9th level, you become immune to being charmed or frightened (but can still accumulate Shadow points from Dread and Sorcery).
Source: Lord of the Rings p. 49

feature.name: Extra Attack Improvement
feature.text:
The number of attacks increases to three when you reach 10th level in this calling.
Source: Lord of the Rings p. 49

feature.name: Champion Way: Sharp-Shooter
feature.text:
"That was a mighty shot in the dark, my friend!"
As King Bard proved, well-placed arrow shots can slay dragons and restore lost kingdoms. You decided to follow his path by mastering ranged weapons.
Source: Lord of the Rings p. 49

feature.name: Bonus Proficiency (Sharp-Shooter)
feature.text:
When you choose this way at 3rd level, you gain proficiency in the Perception skill. If you are already proficient, you add double your proficiency bonus to checks you make with it.
Source: Lord of the Rings p. 50

feature.name: Mighty Shot (Sharp-Shooter)
feature.text:
Starting at 3rd level, you have learned to put all your might into your shots. Before you make an attack with a ranged weapon, you can choose to roll the weapon's damage die and subtract the number rolled from the attack roll. If the attack hits, you roll two additional weapon damage dice on the damage roll. You can deal this extra damage only once per turn.
Source: Lord of the Rings p. 50

feature.name: True Shot (Sharp-Shooter)
feature.text:
By 7th level, when you take the Attack action and attack with a ranged weapon on your turn, you can forgo one of your attacks. If you do so, the next hit you score with a ranged weapon before the end of your turn is a critical hit.
Source: Lord of the Rings p. 50

feature.name: Champion Way: Slayer
feature.text:
"The day will come when they will perish and I shall go back!"
You have chosen a brutal path, maybe because you are looking to avenge a wrong you suffered. For you, the sound of battle is a joyful call.
Source: Lord of the Rings p. 50

feature.name: Sterner Than Steel (Slayer)
feature.text:
When you choose this way at 3rd level, your hit point maximum increases by 3 and increases by 1 again whenever you gain a level in the Champion calling.
Source: Lord of the Rings p. 50

feature.name: Battle-Fury (Slayer)
feature.text:
Starting at 3rd level, you can throw aside all concern for defense to attack with fierce desperation. When you make your first attack on your turn, you can decide to attack recklessly. Doing so gives you advantage on melee weapon attack rolls using Strength, a bonus to damage rolls equal to half your proficiency bonus (rounded down), and resistance to bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage until the start of your next turn, but attack rolls against you have advantage until your next turn.
Source: Lord of the Rings p. 50

feature.name: War-Hardened (Slayer)
feature.text:
By 7th level, your instincts are so honed that you have advantage on initiative rolls, Strength checks, and Strength saving throws, and you cannot be surprised. To gain this benefit, you cannot be blinded, deafened, or incapacitated.
Source: Lord of the Rings p. 50
